title: Notation
body_md:
To enhance readability, we commonly use the superscript $+$ to indicate a one-step forward-shift of a variable. Higher-order forward-shifts and backward-shifts are, in contrast, written using bracketed subscripts. Thus, for $\alpha\geq0$, $u_{[\alpha]}$ denotes the $\alpha$th forward-shift of the variable $u$, whereas $u_{[-\alpha]}$ denotes its $\alpha$th backward-shift. The corresponding forward- and backward-shift operator denoted by $\delta^\alpha$ and $\delta^{-\alpha}$ can act on variables as well as functions, see e.g. \cite{DiwoldKolarSchoberl:2020} for details.
    When a variable consists of several components, i.e., $y=(y^1,\ldots,y^m)$, we write $y_{[\alpha]}=(y^1_{[\alpha]},\ldots,y^m_{[\alpha]})$.
    Shifts of different orders are represented compactly using multi-indices. Let $S_1=(s_{1,1},\ldots,s_{1,m})$ and $S_2=(s_{2,1},\ldots,s_{2,m})$ be two multi-indices. Then, $y_{[-S_1]}$ and $y_{[S_2]}$ denote the corresponding backward- and forward-shifts of the individual components of $y$, respectively. Furthermore, $y_{[-S_1,S_2]}$ is an abbreviation for $y$ together with its backward-shifts up to the orders $S_1$ and its forward-shifts up to the orders $S_2$.

title: Remark
body_md:
As already mentioned, the particular structure of $y$ and its forward-shifts in \eqref{eq:proof_prop_prolonged} represents the specialization to forward-flat systems of the more general form derived in \cite{KolarDiwoldGstottnerSchoeberl:2022} for flat systems that may also involve backward-shifts.
            In that work, the main objective was to derive a quasistatic-like feedback for the purpose of trajectory tracking.
            In the present contribution, however, we focus on dynamic feedback linearization and show that the required dynamic extension is of a particularly simple type, namely prolongations of suitably transformed inputs.

label: eq:dim_argument_forward
title: Proof
body_md:
First, we prove that \eqref{eq:y_backward_transformed} defines a diffeomorphism. Since the backward-shifts of a flat output up to an arbitrary order are functionally independent, it remains to show that the $\#(R_1-\lambda+1)+n+m$ variables $\bar{\zeta}_{[-R_{1}+\lambda-1,-1]}, x, u$ can be expressed in terms of the $\#R_1+m$ backward-shifts $y_{[-R_{1},0]}$.
            Using the identity $\#(\lambda-1)=n$ from item (iii) in Proposition \ref{prop:properties_backward_flat}, it can be shown with
            \begin{equation*}\label{eq:dim_argument_forward}
        		\#(R_1-\lambda+1)+n+m =\# R_1+m
        	\end{equation*}
            that the dimensions indeed match.        
            Again, the diffeomorphism \eqref{eq:y_backward_transformed} is just the inverse of the parameterizing map of the prelonged system \eqref{eq:prelonged_sys} with $\bar g_1=\varphi_{1,[-\lambda_1+1]}(x,u),\ldots,\bar g_s=\varphi_{s,[-\lambda_s+1]}(\bar\zeta_{1,[-r_{1,1}+\lambda_1-1,-1]},\ldots,\bar\zeta_{s-1,[-r_{1,s-1}+\lambda_{s-1}-1,-1]},x)$. Therefore, the prelonged system is static feedback linearizable, because the corresponding parameterizing map is also a diffeomorphism.

title: Remark
body_md: As in the forward-flat case, the map \eqref{eq:y_backward_transformed} can be used to transform the static feedback linearizable prelonged system \eqref{eq:prelonged_sys} into Brunovsky normal form.
